For every 'closures' and 'inner_classes' entry it renames the child to parent.name + '.' + child.name via _replace and pushes it back, so nesting is handled to any depth. For methods of a renamed inner class it sets classname=named.name, which fixes method ownership. Review points: (1) The worklist uses pop() from the end, so output order is reversed or interleaved relative to source order. Check whether sorted_results (line 59) or callers rely on that order. (2) Methods are pushed with their own unqualified name. Confirm that this is intended and that only classname carries the qualification. (3) A method pushed back onto the worklist is processed again, so its own closures are flattened with the method name as the prefix. That prefix lacks the class qualifier, so check the resulting names. radon/visitors.py (visit_FunctionDef near 268-292, visit_ClassDef near 297-331) builds the closures and inner_classes lists with a sub-visitor. Confirm that the Function and Class namedtuples (fields at lines 24 and 36) expose the attributes that getattr(..., ()) expects. Also check that closure complexity is deliberately excluded from the parent's score (the #68 comment). radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py do not take part in this flattening. Review them only for any code that consumes the flattened block names or line ranges, such as per-block raw or Halstead metrics. Make sure they tolerate dotted names and duplicates.

78	def add_inner_blocks(blocks):
79	    '''Process a list of blocks by adding all closures and inner classes as
80	    top-level blocks.
81	    '''
82	    new_blocks = []
83	    all_blocks = blocks[:]
84	    while all_blocks:
85	        block = all_blocks.pop()
86	        new_blocks.append(block)
87	        for inner_block in ('closures', 'inner_classes'):
88	            for i_block in getattr(block, inner_block, ()):
89	                named = i_block._replace(name=block.name + '.' + i_block.name)
90	                all_blocks.append(named)
91	                for meth in getattr(named, 'methods', ()):
92	                    m_named = meth._replace(classname=named.name)
93	                    all_blocks.append(m_named)
94	    return new_blocks
